venue.name: Royal Roads University
venue.description: Royal Roads University is a public applied research university whose main Colwood campus sits at 2005 Sooke Road, about 25 minutes from downtown Victoria, on the traditional Lands of the Lekwungen speaking Peoples, the Songhees and Esquimalt Nations. The campus is set within Hatley Park National Historic Site, surrounded by old growth forest and trails on the shore of the Pacific, and it includes a 5.26 acre walled former Edwardian kitchen garden now being rebuilt as the Farm at RRU. For school, club and community groups the university offers a guided group tour of the campus, requested through an online form on a weekday with at least three business days notice. The gardens and the castle tour at Hatley Park are run separately and are covered by their own record.

facility_notes.bus_parking: Pay parking is in effect on the Royal Roads University campus 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Parking on campus is restricted to designated parking zones, as shown on the campus map. Short term parking of up to one week is paid at a kiosk in the upper, lower, central and west parking lots or through a parking app.

venue.hours_notes: Tours are typically offered between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

programs.name: Guided group tour of the Colwood campus
programs.description: A guided walking tour of the oceanfront Colwood campus for a class, club or organisation, taking in the university buildings, the sustainable gardens and the grounds of Hatley Park National Historic Site. Tours are requested through an online form, which asks you to select a weekday at least 10 business days from today and says tours are typically offered between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. The form asks how many are coming, how long the group has available with options from up to 1 hour through to more than 2 hours, whether you would rather see the Colwood campus or the Langford campus, and how the group will travel, listing school or charter bus among the choices. When it asks the age of the group the only choices offered are grades 9 to 10, grades 11 to 12, post secondary students, adults or community group, and mixed group. Nothing on the site states a price, a fixed tour length or a group size limit.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the campus on foot with a guide, past the university buildings and the sustainable gardens, on the grounds of a national historic site edged by old growth forest and ocean.
programs.our_note: When their own form asks how old your group is, the youngest choice on the list is grades 9 to 10, so this is pitched at teenagers deciding where to go to university rather than at young children. If you want to bring a primary class or a daycare, say so in the form and ask what they would actually show them. Nothing is published about the price or how long a tour runs, and every lot on campus is pay parking around the clock, so budget for that too.
programs.practical_summary: Booked through an online form, on a weekday, at least 10 business days ahead, normally somewhere between 8:30 in the morning and 4:30 in the afternoon. Price, tour length, group size, washrooms, indoor lunch space, rain backup and coach parking are all unstated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Pay parking is in effect on the Royal Roads University campus 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
programs.evidence: Bring your class, club, or organization for a guided group tour of our stunning oceanfront campus.

programs.name: Visit to the Farm at RRU
programs.description: The Farm at RRU is a 5.26 acre former walled Edwardian kitchen garden being rebuilt as a Giving Garden, Market Garden, Indigenous Medicine Garden and polyculture orchard. The university describes it as a gathering place for the community with free workshops and volunteer opportunities, a living lab for student courses and research, and a food production centre supplying fresh fruit, vegetables and herbs to community partners and students. The campus page invites people to get in touch to volunteer, take a tour or otherwise get involved, through a contact form. No age range, price, length, group size or schedule for a visit is published on the university's own pages. The Farm keeps a separate website of its own with an events list, which was not read for this record.
programs.our_note: There is no set visit here to book. The page simply invites you to write and ask, so treat it as a conversation rather than a booking, and say up front how old your group is. The workshop and event dates live on the Farm's own separate website rather than the university one.
programs.practical_summary: A walled garden and orchard on the campus, reached by asking through a contact form. Nothing is published about price, age, group size, washrooms, lunch space or when a group could come.
programs.evidence: Contact us to volunteer at the Farm, take a tour or get involved.

gaps: Hatley Park Formal Gardens and the Hatley Castle guided walking tour sit on this campus but are run and published separately on hatleypark.ca, and they have their own record. This record deliberately covers only what Royal Roads itself offers a visiting group, which is the guided campus tour and an invitation to ask about the Farm
no price is published for a group campus tour. The site never says whether it is free or charged, so no cost was recorded and the record falls below the publishable bar on that alone

no age or grade range is published as a rule for the group tour. The only age signal anywhere on the site is the booking form's own question about the group, whose lowest option is grades 9 to 10, followed by grades 11 to 12, post secondary, adults or community group, and mixed group. That is a strong hint the tour is built for senior secondary students and up, but it is not a stated minimum, so no grade range was recorded and whether daycares are welcome is left unanswered rather than recorded as no

no tour length is published. The form asks how long the group has available, offering up to 1 hour, 1 to 1.5 hours, 1.5 to 2 hours, more than 2 hours, or flexible, which is the group's availability rather than the length of the tour
no maximum or minimum group size is published. The form asks for an anticipated number of participants

the ten business days notice was corrected during verification. A plain fetch returned an older copy of the booking form saying three business days; a live cache bypassed read of the same address gives 10 business days and a different, longer set of questions. The 10 business day figure is the one recorded
no adult to child ratio and no free adult allowance are published
washrooms, an indoor lunch space and a wet weather plan are not addressed anywhere on the campus pages

bus parking and coach drop off are not addressed on any page. The parking pages cover cars, pay parking zones and permits only. The booking form does list school or charter bus as a way to arrive and says the answer helps them plan arrival and parking, so a coach is clearly expected, but no coach parking is described
wheelchair and stroller access on the tour route are not stated. The tour request form invites you to mention accessibility needs, which is not the same as a published answer
the tour request form is the only booking route published and it ends in a CAPTCHA, so no direct booking email address could be recorded
the three business days notice is the form's own instruction to choose a date at least that far ahead; the site does not say whether it is a hard minimum
no youth camps, school outreach or classroom visits for children were found anywhere on the university's site
the Farm at RRU keeps a separate website of its own for events and workshops. It is a different domain, so nothing from it was extracted
the university home page publishes no open graph image and its photographs are of adult students in classrooms, so the hero here is the campus path photograph from the Colwood campus page
no coordinates are published on the site, so the street address was captured and the map pin is left for the geocoding backfill

RETRIEVAL NOTE: several royalroads.ca pages return their body text to a plain fetch but drop every link, and a few return nothing at all. The booking form address and the Farm links here were read in a browser. A fetch only re-run will look thinner than the site really is
